steps.summary: AdoCbl Co-C bond homolysis forms a 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical/cobalamin radical-pair state; this record deliberately leaves the disputed source oxidation-state labels unresolved.
The adenosyl radical abstracts hydrogen from the bound acyl-CoA substrate to initiate the substrate radical.
The substrate radical undergoes the source-proposed intramolecular addition and proton-coupled rearrangement involving His244.
The source-proposed cyclic radical intermediate opens to complete the carbon-skeleton rearrangement, with proton transfer assigned to His244.
The rearranged substrate radical takes hydrogen back from 5'-deoxyadenosine, yielding product and regenerating the adenosyl radical.
Radical-pair recombination restores the AdoCbl cofactor state.

steps.summary: In one half-reaction, the Mn(III)-centered enzyme accepts an electron from superoxide, releases O2, and forms a Mn(II)-centered state.

steps.summary: In the preferred source proposal, Glu166 activates a conserved water relay that deprotonates Ser70 (P62593 natural Ser68) as it attacks the beta-lactam carbonyl to form a tetrahedral intermediate.
Collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate opens the beta-lactam C-N bond and leaves the substrate covalently acylated to Ser70, with the source assigning coupled proton transfer through Ser130.
The source proposal resets the Ser130/Glu166 proton network through water before deacylation.
Glu166 activates water for nucleophilic attack on the acyl-enzyme carbonyl, forming a second tetrahedral intermediate.
Collapse of the second tetrahedral intermediate cleaves the acyl-enzyme bond, releases hydrolyzed product, and regenerates Ser70/Glu166 states.
